title: Spike (2 days): what Prospectus must add before a shared-tier site can be sold with no human step
description:
Outcome: Answer, with the Prospectus session (tell it before anything merges there; its approval is needed for Prospectus changes), what Prospectus offers today and what it must add. Read so far (Prospectus develop 8b8e6b8, 2026-11-07): products are a reviewed file per site (accounts/papyrus-sites.json: one Cognito client, issuer and review id per Papyrus site); billing lines are per product per account with interval plans and "pricing out of scope" (docs/BILLING.md); Stripe is not built; billing "never grants, disables or suspends an entitlement" (no automatic suspension); the weekly quota with check, usage and reservation routes is built (docs/QUOTA.md); cost accounting in microdollars with per-deployment attribution and a split of shared resources by reported usage is agreed but not built (docs/COST_ACCOUNTING.md); lifecycle events (kanbus-6efecd) are a wait. Questions: (1) one "papyrus" product with one deployment per site instead of a product per site? (2) usage-priced plans and how metered usage becomes invoice lines; (3) an event when a payment fails and when an account cancels, and whether a past-due account is suspended automatically (owner decision); (4) does the per-deployment cost ledger accept Papyrus's daily per-tenant usage report for shared resources; (5) pairwise reader identity per site when every site shares one product. Output: a list of Prospectus issues (kanbus ids) with owners, and an update to the Papyrus wait task PPY-a1e75a.

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): Read-only: the Prospectus repository (develop) docs/BILLING.md, docs/QUOTA.md, docs/COST_ACCOUNTING.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, accounts/papyrus-sites.json; Papyrus lib/tenant-keys.ts (tenantIdForProspectusAccount), lib/prospectus-tenant.ts.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: none (spike); produces the inputs for features_backend/tenant-provisioning.feature):
Scenario: Every Prospectus dependency of the shared tier is named
    Given the five questions above
    When the spike closes
    Then each has an answer and, where Prospectus must change, a kanbus issue id

Dependencies: blocked by nothing. Blocks PPY-70a429, PPY-2321aa, PPY-d7274f, PPY-3fd951, PPY-5219fc. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: PPY-a1e75a.

Testing: None (reading and conversation).
Rollout: None.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: Papyrus builds provisioning against a Prospectus contract that changes. Mitigation: every Papyrus task that calls Prospectus waits on a named, deployed Prospectus route (same rule as PPY-a1e75a).

Releasable on its own: not applicable (spike).
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: unchanged.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).

comments.author: home
comments.text: Prospectus session answered (2026-11-08, checked on Prospectus develop and main). (1) Products: no single papyrus product with deployments today; each site is its own product papyrus-<site> with its own Cognito pool/client/compute role, a reviewed entry in accounts/papyrus-sites.json capped at 40 (5 used). No self-serve provisioning: account creation grants only the caller's own product; staff can toggle a product for an account from the CRM but no product can via API; membership needs an already-enrolled Person, no invite by email. Open Prospectus cards: kanbus-59284c (provisioning/invite API), kanbus-4c99c6, kanbus-b09c91, kanbus-db57cb. One papyrus product with API-created tenant deployments held as data would be a NEW model needing Ryan's direction and its own security review. (2) Lifecycle events: none published; kanbus-6efecd (entitlement.changed) is open. Billing never changes access by design (docs/BILLING.md decision 7, kanbus-8e3174 no automatic access changes); past-due only creates a CRM follow-up. Our '14 days past due then read-only' rule contradicts that decision: Ryan must change it first. Stripe not built; invoice/payment ledger built but off. (3) Metering: the weekly quota service (docs/QUOTA.md) is live for Babulus only. docs/COST_ACCOUNTING.md (merged 2026-11-06, epic kanbus-bb0b6c) is design only: real-dollar private cost per Account/app/deployment/category/day, usage batched about once a minute to an SQS queue via a shared sender library, every AWS resource tagged anthus:app / anthus:account (Account UUID or shared) / anthus:deployment, daily Cost Explorer import, quota drawn against real cost (weekly budget = plan monthly amount / 4). Correction: billing is NOT usage-based today (plan per deployment; quota limits usage; nothing charges for overage). Usage billing is a new commercial decision. Ask for PPY-3fd951: use namespaced item kinds (openai.tokens.input, jev.tokens), name the tenant by Prospectus Account UUID plus a deployment id, tag shared multi-tenant resources anthus:account=shared. Spike conclusion: Prospectus needs (a) API-created deployments of one papyrus product, (b) lifecycle events (kanbus-6efecd), (c) Ryan's decision on automatic access changes from billing, (d) usage billing beyond quota, (e) the cost accounting build (kanbus-bb0b6c).

comments.text: Answers from the Prospectus session (2026-11-08): each site today is product 'papyrus-<site>' with its own pool, client and compute role in accounts/papyrus-sites.json (cap about 40); no self-serve provisioning API; no invite by email (kanbus-59284c, kanbus-4c99c6, kanbus-b09c91, kanbus-db57cb); no lifecycle events (kanbus-6efecd); billing is a plan per deployment, not usage; the weekly quota service is live for Babulus only; cost accounting is designed (docs/COST_ACCOUNTING.md, epic kanbus-bb0b6c: private real-dollar cost per Account/app/deployment/category/day, usage batched to an SQS queue by a shared sender library, anthus:app/anthus:account/anthus:deployment tags, daily Cost Explorer import) and Ryan said build it and test it on our sites and the design partner's three new sites. Ryan decided (2026-11-08): one 'papyrus' product with tenant deployments created by API as data (question 1 answered yes); the lifecycle rule is accepted (question 3); overage billing is wanted. Filed: PPY-966ef5, PPY-6cb44b, PPY-8a3c6a, PPY-25e0d7. Remaining open: question 5 (pairwise reader subjects per deployment).

comments.text:
Answered 2026-11-08 from the Prospectus board (develop a329ee1), so this spike closes:
(1) One papyrus product with a deployment per site: yes, epic kanbus-b770c2 (kanbus-271b4a records and API; dedicated sites keep the per-site registry).
(2) Usage-priced plans: the quota now runs on real cost in microdollars, weekly budget = monthly amount / 4 (kanbus-c7be53, merged); usage beyond the quota has no Prospectus design yet (Papyrus PPY-8a3c6a, off the M7 path).
(3) Payment-failed, past-due and cancellation events and automatic access change: yes; decision 7 superseded in Prospectus docs/BILLING.md; standing derived (kanbus-b19d5a) and published through kanbus-6efecd.
(4) Shared-resource split by Papyrus's per-tenant usage: yes, kanbus-f45f7f (one papyrus queue, ledger checks deployment ownership) on top of the merged ledger kanbus-6efec6.
(5) Pairwise reader identity per site with one product: yes, reader subjects become pairwise per deployment (kanbus-3e5e82).
Remaining asks moved to PPY-966ef5: deployment.changed event, changed-since list cursor, single-writer rules for deployments and hostnames.
